body:
In Georgia, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$2,940 to $7,860** in 2026, or $1.47 to $3.93 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in Georgia actually earn: a median of $23.24 an hour, 2% below the national median of $23.75.

| | Georgia | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.47 to $3.93 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $2,940 to $7,860 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $23.24 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## Georgia exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in Georgia |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,205 to $5,895 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $2,940 to $7,860 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $3,675 to $9,825 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $4,410 to $11,790 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in Georgia's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in Georgia's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell | $23.83 | $3,008 to $8,022 |
| Savannah | $22.14 | $2,837 to $7,566 |
| Augusta-Richmond County | $19.75 | $2,596 to $6,922 |
| Athens-Clarke County | $19.74 | $2,595 to $6,919 |

The gap between Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell and Athens-Clarke County is $4.09 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $413 to $1,102 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in Georgia

**Siding.** Stucco leads on new homes in the South Atlantic region, which includes Georgia: it was the most common wall material on new single-family homes started in 2023, at 39.4%, based on Census data analyzed by NAHB. Stucco takes more paint per square foot than smooth siding and is usually sprayed and back-rolled, so stucco houses tend to land in the upper half of the range. Wood and fiber cement siding fall in the middle.

**Weather and timing.** Cold is rarely the problem here; rain and humidity are. Sherwin-Williams says the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window, and paint needs dry weather to cure, so a good painter watches the forecast and works around storms. Spring and fall are the easiest seasons. In midsummer, crews often start early and avoid walls in full afternoon sun.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in Georgia

Licensing for painting-only work is mostly a local matter in Georgia, so ask your city or county building department what applies where you live. Whatever the rules, ask every painter for a certificate of liability insurance, and check that it is current.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. Georgia is one of the states EPA authorizes to run its own Renovation, Repair and Painting program, so painters who disturb old paint there are certified through the state program instead of EPA. Ask to see the certification before work starts.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by Georgia's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**Georgia rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $23.24 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 0.983**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in Georgia?

About $2,940 to $7,860 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell expect more, about $3,008 to $8,022.

### Where in Georgia is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell has the highest painter wages at $23.83 an hour, and Athens-Clarke County the lowest at $19.74. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in Georgia?

Spring and fall are easiest. You need about 48 hours of dry weather after each coat, so a painter will schedule around rain and avoid walls in full summer sun.

### Do I need a licensed painter in Georgia?

It depends on your city or county, so ask your local building department. Either way, ask for proof of liability insurance.
